rationales: Input is data supplied to an algorithm, not its starting symbol or point.
Goto is a control instruction, not the starting point of an algorithm.
Set assigns a value and does not mark an algorithm’s start.
Start identifies the beginning of an algorithm.
Data Hosting Computer Protocol is not the expansion of DHCP.
Dynamic Host Computer Protocol is not the expansion of DHCP.
DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
Dynamic Host Common Protocol is not the expansion of DHCP.
Routers connect multiple networks and direct traffic between them.
Channels carry signals but are not what routers connect together.
Addresses identify devices or destinations rather than being connected by routers.
Layers are parts of a network model, not the networks routers connect.
Hacking can be a cybercrime when it involves unauthorized access.
Phishing is a cybercrime that uses deceptive messages to steal information.
Identity theft is a cybercrime involving the misuse of someone’s identity.
Decryption is the process of converting encrypted data back to readable form and is not inherently a cybercrime.
A password of at least eight characters is generally considered stronger than a short one.
A good password should not contain the username.
Including uppercase letters can make a password stronger.
Using only your name makes a password easy to guess and is not a good characteristic.
Data is represented and stored in computer memory as bits.
A byte is a group of bits, not the basic form in which data is represented.
A word is a group of bits processed as a unit, not the basic form of stored data.
A character is encoded using bits rather than being the basic storage form.
The <title> tag specifies a page title, not a paragraph.

The

tag is used to define a paragraph.
The <hr> tag inserts a thematic break, not a paragraph.

The
tag inserts a line break, not a paragraph.

The
tag is a void tag and does not require a closing tag.

The

tag normally has both opening and closing tags.
The <body> tag normally has both opening and closing tags.
The <head> tag normally has both opening and closing tags.
An algorithm consists of steps, but it produces an output.
Terminal is a flowchart symbol, not what an algorithm produces.
An algorithm processes input to produce a defined output.
Analysis is a problem-solving activity, not what an algorithm produces.
The terminal symbol represents the start or end of a flowchart.
A connector links different parts of a flowchart.
A process symbol represents an operation or instruction.
A decision symbol represents a condition with alternative paths.
Problem solving is the process of working through difficult or complex problems.
Defining a problem is one step in solving it, not the whole process.
Using guesses is only one possible technique, not the name of the process.
Acting it out is a particular strategy, not the general process.
Secondary memory can store data whether or not it is currently important.
Secondary memory is not defined by the expense of its data storage.
Temporary storage is characteristic of volatile memory, not secondary memory.
Secondary memory retains data for long-term storage.
In the usual binary measurement used in this context, 1024 bytes equal 1 kilobyte.
1024 bytes are not equal to 1 megabyte.
1024 bytes are not equal to 1 terabyte.
1024 bytes are not equal to 1 gigabyte.
A prototype can help test an idea early and save time in development.
Analysis helps understand a problem but is not the intended answer here.
A candidate solution may address a problem, but it is not the answer to this item.
Start is a flowchart label and does not help save time by itself.
The expression shows multiplication distributed over addition, which is the distributive law.
The associative law changes grouping, not the distribution shown here.
The commutative law changes the order of terms or factors.
Conductive law is not the name of this Boolean algebra law.
